verbs.text: Stretched as far as the eye could see
Blazed pink in the dawn light

sentences.text: Majestic, snow-capped peaks soared into the clouds, indifferent to the valley and everyone in it.
The mountain reared above the valley, its lower slopes dark with pine, its summit lost in cloud.
A sheer, ice-glazed precipice dropped away beneath their feet into a silence so deep that it seemed to pull at them.
A narrow, stony track zigzagged up the mountainside, doubling back on itself a dozen times before the pass.
A bitter, scouring wind howled across the ridge, and they crawled the last hundred metres on hands and knees.
Loose, treacherous scree slid beneath his boots and went clattering into the void.
One misplaced step on the narrow, crumbling ledge, and she would have plunged into the ravine.
With a roar that shook the valley, the avalanche thundered down the slope, snapping pines like matchsticks.
Thick, swirling mist shrouded the summit, and the cairns that marked the path vanished one by one.
Her shout echoed around the valley and returned to her, smaller each time, until the silence closed over it.
A mountain goat bounded from rock to rock as though the cliff were a staircase.
An eagle circled on the rising air, scanning the slopes for the slightest movement.
Sheep grazed on the lower slopes, where the gentle, grassy foothills gave way to bare rock.
From the summit, range upon range stretched as far as the eye could see, fading from slate to the palest blue.
The vast, luminous glacier glittered in the sunlight, a frozen river a thousand years in the making.
Jagged, serrated crags loomed over the village and kept it in shadow for half the year.
A thread of meltwater trickled down the hillside between clumps of purple, wind-combed heather.
At sunrise the highest pinnacle blazed pink in the dawn light, and she drew the thin, crystalline air deep into her lungs.
A few stunted, weathered pines clung to the rock face, their roots gripping cracks no wider than a finger.
Nothing grew on the bleak, barren summit; there was only rock, wind and an immense, humbling sky.
Far below lay a deep, shadowed valley, a river winding through it like a dropped silver thread.
The path led into a dark, forbidding gorge where the sun never reached and the air tasted of wet stone.
Colossal, lichen-crusted boulders lay scattered across the hillside, abandoned there by some ancient glacier.
No one had crossed the remote, snowbound pass since the first falls of winter.
They floundered through deep, powdery snowdrifts that swallowed them to the thigh.
Hail lashed the exposed slope, and the rope between them hummed in the wind.
The climbers whooped and called to one another as they hauled themselves up the last few metres.
A crevasse yawned at their feet, blue-black and bottomless.
In the evening the peaks turned rose, then violet, and a profound stillness settled over the valley.
Thunder reverberated between the peaks, each crash overtaken by its own echo.
